upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm looking to claim for. His name is Alex and he's 9 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to hear about Alex.

Now, could you tell me: are you responsible for Alex? This means he lives with you, or you're contributing to the cost of looking after him at least the same amount as Child Benefit would provide (currently £25.60 per week for an eldest or only child).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives with me at home. I'm his parent and I look after him full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you for confirming.

Next, could you tell me where you and Alex live? Specifically, are you living in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we live in Manchester, so we're in England.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Lovely, thank you for confirming that.

One more question: Is Alex a British citizen, or does he have the right to live in the UK? Also, has he been in the UK for at least the last 3 months (unless he's a British or Irish citizen, or a family member of one)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is a British citizen, so that shouldn't be a problem.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions: What is your nationality or immigration status? For example, are you a British or Irish citizen, or do you have settled or pre-settled status, or another type of visa or permission to live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen as well.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that.

One final question: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex? Only one person can claim Child Benefit for the same child at a time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me looking after him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you appear to be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

**For Alex (age 9):**
- ✅ He is under 16, meeting the age requirement
- ✅ You are responsible for him as his parent and he lives with you
- ✅ You both live in the United Kingdom (England)
- ✅ Alex is a British citizen with the right to live in the UK
- ✅ You are a British citizen, meeting the immigration status requirements
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex

**Next steps:** If you'd like to make a claim, you can do so online through the official government website or by post using the Child Benefit claim form (CH2).

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
